Hi Sean / Kimberly —

Thanks for the call this morning. Procurement still needs a clear list of what Redwood will hand over as "proof-of-processing" during the pilot and what will sit behind an escrow / audit-only channel. To be explicit: we need an itemised evidence matrix that maps the processing steps -> artefact types (logs, redactable traces, KV cache attestations) -> retention window and the expected delivery mechanism (SFTP, signed report, or DocuSign acknowledgement).

Two immediate asks from MedicoCorp legal:
- Confirm whether subprocessor identities for EU routing are available as a signed snapshot (we need the vendor legal name + country + control owner).
- Confirm whether Redwood will agree to a TIA sampling cadence (initial weekly sample for 4 weeks, then monthly) and the level of data redaction applied to samples.

Can you provide a one-page summary and the technical flow diagram by COB Wed Aug 11? Chris from procurement is copied — he will confirm the DocuSign cadence once we confirm the handoff channel.

--
Elaine Tucker
Head of Procurement, MedicoCorp
elaine.tucker@medicorp.com

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Tucker <elaine.tucker@medicorp.com>; kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Scoped TIA evidence path + escrow & subprocessor confirmation for MedicoPilot

Elaine — thanks, clear asks. Attaching an internal snapshot and a proposed evidence matrix (high level) in the next email. Quick answers inline:

1) Subprocessor snapshot: yes — we can provide a signed CSV that lists vendor legal name, country of processing, and a Redwood control owner. That will be a point-in-time attestation (we'll include a hash and a sign-off).

2) TIA sampling cadence: the proposed plan (we are OK) — weekly samples for the first 4 weeks, then monthly. Samples will be redacted to remove patient-identifiable fields; we'll provide a redaction schema and an audit hash for traceability.

Open question for legal: do you need full request/response token payloads, or are transaction-level metadata records adequate for your audit? Metadata would include timestamp, route (EU/US cluster ID), model ID, and truncated request hash. Full payloads require narrower legal hooks.

I'll circulate the flow diagram and the matrix in 30 mins.

Cheers,
Sean
Security & Trust, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Scoped TIA evidence path + escrow & subprocessor confirmation for MedicoPilot

Forwarding the flow diagram and the initial evidence matrix. Attachment stubs below.

Attachments:
- dataflow_map_v2.png (image/png) — shows routing surfaces, caching tiers, and where escrow snapshots are taken.
- tia_scope_table.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) — high-level matrix mapping artefact -> retention -> delivery channel.
- subprocessor_snapshot_20260806.csv (text/csv) — point-in-time vendor list with Redwood control owner.

Key notes on the diagram and matrix (short):
- We segregate European customer traffic at the ingress layer (EU edge cluster) and maintain a signed routing token at cache checkpoint CP-2. That checkpoint is where we record a lightweight trace (request ID + truncated hash) and copy metadata to an audit channel.
- Escrow channel: we propose SFTP with an HMAC-signed manifest for each delivery. DocuSign will be used only for attestation of the signed manifest, not for daily deliveries.
- Redaction: PII fields are replaced with deterministic salt+hash. We can provide salts to your legal under an NDA if you need re-identification for IR (rare).

Happy to jump on a 20 min call if you want to walk the diagram.

-Jonas
From: legal@medicorp.com
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai; kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Elaine Tucker <elaine.tucker@medicorp.com>, Chris Potter <chris.potter@procurex.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 14:07:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Scoped TIA evidence path + escrow & subprocessor confirmation for MedicoPilot

Sean / Jonas — thanks for the materials. A few clarifying points from MedicoCorp legal before we confirm the DocuSign path:

1) The CSV snapshot looks good but we need each vendor's country of incorporation as well as country of actual processing for any vendor that has multi-region facilities. Please update the snapshot to include both fields.

2) For the weekly samples: we require a checkbox-style attestation (DocuSign) that confirms redaction schema used and that no raw PII was shared. We understand you want DocuSign for manifests — we need a way to tie the attestation to the specific sample batch (sample manifest ID).

3) Regarding escrow access: MedicoCorp will need an audited access log for any time our auditors retrieve escrowed artefacts. Can Redwood provide a signed access log (with operator identity) and an HSM-backed timestamp?

Please respond with updated CSV and a sample signed manifest template. If you can provide the signed snapshot and manifest template by COB Wed Aug 11 (your timezone), we can route to procurement for final cadence confirmation.

- Olivia Park
Senior Counsel, MedicoCorp
legal@medicorp.com

Olivia / Elaine / Chris —

Acknowledged. Action items we completed and attachments provided:
- Updated subprocessor snapshot (subprocessor_snapshot_20260811.csv) uploaded to the Drive link in related_links — includes country of incorporation + country of processing for multi-region vendors. (See attachment stub in this thread.)
- Sample signed manifest template: we attach an example (manifest_example.txt) and include an HMAC field + manifest_id pattern. Manifests are HMAC-signed using a Redwood key; we can optionally route an audit copy to your escrow SFTP as well.
- Access logs: Redwood can produce operator-level access logs, signed with an HSM timestamp and exported as a gzipped JSONL (each line is a signed statement). We will include a sample access log extract in the drive folder.

Next steps proposed:
1) Legal confirms the manifest format is acceptable for DocuSign attestation.
2) Procurement confirms SFTP endpoint for escrow ingestion (Chris).
3) Schedule a 20-min walk-through on Thu Aug 12 to confirm redaction schema and TIA sample manifest mapping.

If all good, we'll issue the weekly sample for Aug 12 and the first signed manifest on Aug 13.

Thanks — Sean
